params.name: res_m
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths / align_swaths default grid resolution (2.0 m)

params.name: exclude
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths terrain proxy ~isin(classification,(5,6,9)) -- the VENDOR classes, so no CSF run is needed

params.name: tie_modes
params.why: the two estimators coreg.coregister_swaths supports; corrections_geoid.json records swath_tie='intercept' as the pipeline's

params.name: half_width_m
params.why: window half-width for the along-track sweep and the chains. There is NO library default and none is invented here; 400 m is one rung of the ladder in section 2, chosen so the window fits inside a single 2.5 km tile at every along-track sample. Section 2 measures what the choice costs; section 3 is re-runnable at any other rung with --half-width-m

params.name: ladder_half_widths_m
params.why: the window sizes reported in section 2. Chosen to span a factor of 12, from below one flight-line sidelap width to a whole tile; nothing is excluded on their basis, the whole ladder is printed

params.name: shape
params.why: square window. A disk would give a ragged grid edge and fewer cells for the same half-width; localtie supports both and --shape switches it

params.name: mark_radius_m
params.why: radius within which a mark's flight line is identified by return count (groundtruth.chain.covering_lines). It selects WHICH LINE the mark is on, not which marks are used; every mark is reported

params.name: repeat_step_m
params.why: along-track spacing of the within-tile repeat windows in section 3c. 300 m so that neighbouring 400 m-half-width windows overlap and neighbouring 800 m ones overlap heavily; it sets the SAMPLING of the short-range scatter, and excludes nothing

params.name: repeat_half_widths_m
params.why: the two window sizes section 3c repeats at, so that scatter which is estimator noise (shrinks with window) can be told from scatter which is local structure (does not)

params.name: centre
params.why: where each along-track window sits across the overlap strip. 'strip' is the strip's own median easting -- the sidelap middle, where the intercept tie is an interpolation; 'tile' is the overlap cell nearest the tile centre, which on a N-S strip is its western EDGE. Both are run and both are reported; neither is used to exclude anything

params.name: target_line
params.why: the frame the marks are carried into. 137 is the middle Elba line and the one the brief names; --target-line changes it

columns.line: flight line with the most terrain returns within 25.0 m of the mark
columns.links: steps from the gauge line along the adjacent-overlap chain
columns.disagree_mm: elba minus elbaext for that line's constant, mm
columns.per_link_mm: that disagreement divided by sqrt(links), mm
columns.pair: flight-line pair, ref-src; dz is added to src to reach ref's frame
columns.tie_mode: which coreg tie estimator both scatters were measured with
columns.half_width_m: window half-width about each sample location, m
columns.dz_mm: the tie, from coreg.coregister_swaths in the stated tie mode, mm
columns.dz_median_mm: independent check: median of the UNSHIFTED overlap difference, mm
columns.nk_cells: cells the Nuth & Kaeaeb fit used; 0 means the fit was abandoned
columns.ovl_cells: cells where both lines have terrain returns in that window
columns.nmad1_mm: robust scatter left in the overlap after the tie, mm
columns.dtan_lo: smallest across-track coordinate tan(scan_ref)-tan(scan_src) in the window, dimensionless; the intercept tie is read at dtan = 0
columns.dtan_hi: largest across-track coordinate in the window, dimensionless (a difference of tangents)
columns.c_mm_tan: across-track slope fitted with the intercept there, mm per unit tangent
columns.extrap: YES/blank flag: YES when dtan = 0 lies OUTSIDE [dtan_lo, dtan_hi], i.e. the intercept tie is an extrapolation here
columns.degenerate: YES/blank flag: YES when the Nuth & Kaeaeb fit used zero cells, in which case dz is coreg's abandoned-fit 0.0 m
columns.tile: the gen1 tile the window was cut from
columns.northing: northing of the window centre (nearest overlap cell to tile centre), m
columns.d_elba_km: signed along-track distance from the Elba centroid, km
columns.easting: easting of the window centre, m
columns.dz_med_mm: tie for the pair (ref=136, src=137) in that window with tie='overlap_median' -- what to ADD to line 137 to bring it into line 136's frame there, mm
columns.flag_med: D if the Nuth & Kaeaeb fit used zero cells there, X if the window does not sample dtan = 0
columns.dz_int_mm: the same tie with tie='intercept' (LAD intercept at across-track position zero), mm
columns.flag_int: same two flags for the intercept run
columns.dz_plain_mm: median of the UNSHIFTED overlap difference z(136) - z(137) in that window -- no horizontal solution applied, mm
columns.n_windows: windows tied along the (ref=136, src=137) overlap inside 4342-29-64.laz, count
columns.mean_mm: mean of the tie over those windows, mm
columns.sd_mm: standard deviation of the tie between those windows, mm
columns.min_mm: smallest tie among those windows, mm
columns.max_mm: largest tie among those windows, mm
columns.span_km: along-track distance from the first window centre to the last, km
columns.n_long: along-track samples, one window per tile over the corridor, count
columns.sd_long_mm: standard deviation of the tie between them, mm
columns.n_short: windows inside ONE tile, a few hundred metres apart, count
columns.sd_short_mm: standard deviation of the tie between THOSE, mm
columns.F: variance ratio, long-range over short-range, dimensionless
columns.p: one-sided p for that ratio, F(n_long-1, n_short-1)
columns.n_pairs: pairs of along-track samples used for the correlation, count
columns.r_sep_vs_diff: Pearson r between the separation of two samples and the absolute difference of their ties, dimensionless
columns.n_near: how many of its returns are within 25.0 m
columns.path: lines walked from that line to line 137; a single entry means the mark is ALREADY on the target line and no transfer is needed
columns.local_mm: constant to ADD to the mark's line to put it into line 137's frame, measured AT THE MARK, mm
columns.sig_formal_mm: coreg's per-link sigmas in quadrature, mm -- known optimistic
columns.sig_window_mm: per-link window-ladder spreads in quadrature, mm
columns.imported_mm: the same constant implied by elbaext's fitted set (dz[line] - dz[137]), mm
columns.diff_mm: local minus imported, mm -- what the extrapolation costs here
